'''Bruce Eliot Maryanoff''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] (born February 26, 1947, in [[Philadelphia]], [[Pennsylvania]]) is an American medicinal and organic [[chemist]].

==Background and contributions==
<!-- Deleted image removed: [[File:Maryanoff.jpg|thumb|Maryanoff BE]] -->Maryanoff received a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] degree in chemistry in 1969, and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in organic chemistry in 1972, both from [[Drexel University]].<ref>{{citation |title=Biographies of The Drexel 100, 2003 |url=http://drexel.edu/IA/drexel100/drexel-100-class2003.html#docu |publisher=Drexel University |accessdate=2013-05-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130617200927/http://drexel.edu/IA/drexel100/drexel-100-class2003.html#docu |archive-date=June 17, 2013 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> From 1972 to 1974 Maryanoff was a postdoctoral fellow in the department of chemistry at [[Princeton University]]. He joined [[McNeil Laboratories]], Inc., a [[Johnson & Johnson]] subsidiary, in 1974 and advanced on the scientific ladder in various Johnson & Johnson pharmaceutical units to the highest scientific position in the company. Maryanoff retired from [[Johnson & Johnson Pharmaceutical Research & Development]], [[Spring House, Pennsylvania|Spring House]], [[Pennsylvania]], in January 2010. He is now affiliated with [[The Scripps Research Institute]], [[La Jolla]], [[California]] and is a Distinguished Professor at the Baruch S. Blumberg Institute, Doylestown, [[Pennsylvania]]. He served as associate editor for the journal ''[[ACS Medicinal Chemistry Letters]]'' from 2009-2020. He is married to Dr. [[Cynthia A. Maryanoff]].

Maryanoff has been active in the fields of [[medicinal chemistry]] and [[organic chemistry]]. He is an inventor of [[topiramate]],<ref>{{cite patent|country=US|number=4513006|pubdate=1985-04-23|title=Anticonvulsant sulfamate derivatives|assign1=[[McNeil_Consumer_Healthcare|McNeil Laboratories Inc.]]|inventor1-last=Maryanoff|inventor1-first=Bruce E.|inventor2-last=Gardocki|inventor2-first=Joseph F.}}</ref> a unique sugar sulfamate drug, which has been marketed worldwide for the treatment of [[epilepsy]] and [[migraine]], attaining annual sales of more than $2 billion.<ref>{{citation|title=Johnson & Johnson 2008 Annual Report-Major Pharmaceutical Product Revenues, p 36 |url=http://www.jnj.com/connect/about-jnj/publications/?flash=true |publisher=Johnson & Johnson |accessdate=2013-05-04}}</ref> Topiramate is also a principal component of the antiobesity drug [[Qsymia]].<ref name="FDA News Release">{{citation|title=FDA approves weight-management drug Qsymia |url=https://www.fda.gov/NewsEvents/Newsroom/PressAnnouncements/ucm312468.htm |publisher=U.S. Food and Drug Administration, July 17, 2012 |accessdate=September 30, 2012}}{{dead link|date=May 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Maryanoff is an internationally renowned expert in [[drug design]] and [[drug discovery]], especially in the application of [[protein structure]]-based drug design. He made seminal contributions to understanding the [[stereochemistry]] and mechanism of the [[Wittig reaction]]; adapted the cobalt-catalyzed [[alkyne trimerization]] to the synthesis of [[macrocycles]]; and devised novel [[peptides]] that undergo [[self-assembly]] to mimic native [[collagen]] structurally and functionally. Maryanoff is an author on 280 scientific publications, including several books (editor), book chapters, and review articles. He is an inventor on 100 issued U.S. [[patents]], has presented over 185 invited lectures worldwide, and mentored 11 postdoctoral associates. Maryanoff organized and edited a special memorial issue of the ''[[Journal of Medicinal Chemistry]]'' to honor the memory of Dr. [[Paul Janssen]] (2005)<ref name="PAJ Janssen Memorial Issue of J. Med. Chem.">{{citation|title=Janssen Memorial Issue of J. Med. Chem. |url=http://pubs.acs.org/cgi-bin/sample.cgi/jmcmar/2005/48/i06/pdf/jm040193r.pdf |publisher=American Chemical Society, 2005 |accessdate=2008-10-17}}</ref> and has served on numerous editorial advisory boards for scientific journals and research grant review committees.
